title: The Hundred Years’ War
status: Proposed catalogue with one developed historical opening
count_note: The supplied tables contain 12 Edwardian, 14 Caroline/interwar and 11 Lancastrian entries: 37 unique dates. All supplied entries are retained.
implementation_rule: Each developed entry is a dated starting-state reference. Later events depend on simulation and player choices. Historical battles, alliances, accessions, deaths and the end of the war are never scheduled merely because they occurred in recorded history.

entries.title: The War Begins
entries.description: Edward III of England and Philip VI of France enter open conflict over French territories and royal authority.

entries.title: The Flemish Alliance
entries.description: Edward III claims the French crown, campaigns with Flemish support, and concludes the Truce of Espléchin in September.

entries.title: The Breton Succession
entries.description: Brittany splits between rival claimants supported by England and France.

entries.title: The Truce of Malestroit
entries.description: A negotiated suspension of Anglo-French hostilities amid continuing regional tensions.

entries.title: The War Rekindled
entries.description: Major English campaigns resume following the expiry of the truce.

entries.title: Scotland Enters the Campaign
entries.description: David II invades England in support of France; Edward III campaigns in France.

entries.title: The Truce of Calais
entries.description: Calais falls to England and a new Anglo-French truce begins.

entries.title: The Black Prince’s Campaign
entries.description: Large-scale English offensives resume in southern France.

entries.title: The Captive King
entries.description: John II of France is captured at Poitiers, creating a French succession and government crisis.

entries.title: The Truces of Bordeaux and Berwick
entries.description: Anglo-French and Anglo-Scottish truces establish separate diplomatic settlements.
entries.review_note: Exact diplomatic instruments and the ransom/peace character of the Berwick settlement require dated source review before activation.

entries.title: Edward’s Final Edwardian Offensive
entries.description: Failed peace negotiations lead to a major invasion of France.

entries.title: The Peace of Brétigny
entries.description: England and France agree to a major territorial settlement.

entries.title: The Breton Settlement
entries.description: The Battle of Auray resolves the military contest over Brittany’s succession; the 1365 treaty formalizes its settlement.
entries.review_note: A 1364 snapshot must not pre-apply the 1365 treaty.

entries.title: The Castilian Civil War
entries.description: France and England support competing claimants for the Castilian throne.

entries.title: The Caroline War
entries.description: Charles V resumes major Anglo-French hostilities; the victorious Trastámara dynasty becomes an important French ally.

entries.title: The Castilian Intervention
entries.description: Castilian naval power helps France defeat England at La Rochelle.

entries.title: The Portuguese Connection
entries.description: Portugal establishes a formal alliance with England while pursuing its own conflict with Castile.

entries.title: The Truce of Bruges
entries.description: Anglo-French hostilities are suspended after extensive French territorial recovery.

entries.title: The War Resumes
entries.description: The truce expires; Edward III dies and Richard II inherits England.

entries.title: The Scottish and Portuguese Fronts
entries.description: French forces assist Scotland against England; Portugal defeats Castile at Aljubarrota.

entries.title: The Truce of Leulinghem
entries.description: England, France, and their allies enter a prolonged truce.

entries.title: The Great Diplomatic Settlement
entries.description: Anglo-French marriage diplomacy reinforces the long truce.

entries.title: The Lancastrian Accession
entries.description: Henry IV takes the English throne amid deteriorating Anglo-French relations.

entries.title: The Welsh Rebellion
entries.description: Owain Glyndŵr challenges English rule; France subsequently supports the revolt.

entries.title: French Intervention in Wales
entries.description: Anglo-French hostility continues through limited operations despite the wider truce arrangements.
entries.review_note: The supplied title is retained as a proposal. Distinguish 1403 activity from the 1404 alliance and the major French expedition of 1405 before activating a snapshot.

entries.title: England and the French Civil War
entries.description: English forces intervene in France’s Armagnac–Burgundian struggle.

entries.title: The Lancastrian Invasion
entries.description: Henry V prepares to take his expedition across the Channel. Begin before departure; the campaign’s course and outcomes remain open.
entries.source_description: Henry V invades France; the campaign culminates at Agincourt.

entries.title: The Conquest of Normandy
entries.description: Henry V launches a sustained campaign to establish English control over Normandy.

entries.title: The Burgundian Alliance
entries.description: The assassination of John the Fearless helps drive Burgundy into an alliance with England.

entries.title: The Treaty of Troyes
entries.description: Henry V is recognized by the treaty as Charles VI’s successor, but the Dauphin’s supporters continue resisting.

entries.title: The Rival Monarchies
entries.description: Henry V and Charles VI die; the infant Henry VI and Charles VII become rival claimants.

entries.title: The French Resurgence
entries.description: The relief of Orléans and the coronation of Charles VII transform French military and political prospects.

entries.title: The Burgundian Reconciliation
entries.description: Burgundy abandons England and concludes the Treaty of Arras with Charles VII.

entries.title: The Truce of Tours
entries.description: England and France suspend major fighting while diplomatic negotiations continue.

entries.title: The Final War
entries.description: The truce breaks down; France and Brittany launch the campaign to recover Normandy.

entries.title: The Fall of English Normandy
entries.description: French victory at Formigny precedes the completion of Normandy’s reconquest.

entries.title: The Fall of Bordeaux
entries.description: France recaptures Bordeaux following the Battle of Castillon; the Hundred Years’ War effectively ends.
entries.review_note: The historical label never imposes a campaign end date or prevents later simulation.
